2.text: Indeed, what shall I do? Where shall I find any other help? I do not know.

3.text: With your permission I will take you for my ‘assistant.’ Search for me.

4.text: Here I am without any help at all!”

5.text: Then the man pronouncing the incantation picks up any small thing,

6.text: for instance, a splinter of wood, and pretends that it is the Man from the

7.text: Upper Region. Then he demands from the Front Head (the star Arcturus).

8.text: its reindeer-team, and says, “O Front Head! give me your best reindeer-bucks.

9.text: This man will use them for his team.” He demands also from Rulteˊnnin (the

10.text: constellation Orion) his whip. Then the Man from the Upper Region starts on

11.text: his searching journey. First of all he visits the “Ground Beings.” He arrives

12.text: there, and they say, “You have come?” (but in reality the man does not leave

13.text: the place) — “Yes, I have come!” — “Who are you?” — “Oh! I am employed

14.text: only for an ‘assistant.’ I come to ask where that man is. He is here,

15.text: probably!” — “But we do not know anything. It is wholly unknown. We

16.text: cannot tell!” Then he goes away (of course, the man is standing motionless),

17.text: and begins to talk again, and he says, “Oh! where shall I go? Where is he?”

18.text: He goes to the Upper Being (G̣ɪrg̣oˊl-vaˊɪrg̣ɪn). “Oh! you have come.” —

19.text: “Yes!” — “What do you want?” — “I am only on a search. I am an ‘assist-

20.text: ant’ for those people.” — “Indeed! But we do not know. That man did not

21.text: come to us. It is quite unknown!” — “You say so! But where may he be?

22.text: He comes home and finds the patient, who is now dead. He says,

23.text: “Oh, I could not find him! The people yonder do not know about him.

24.text: Oh, it is hard! Where shall I find him? I will go and look among the

25.text: people of Darkness.” He comes to the Darkness. “You have come” —

26.text: “Yes! Oh, oh! There he is!” Here at last he is found by the seeker.

27.text: “Then you are here?” — “Yes! I have come here. Here I am abiding!” —

28.text: “Oh, let us go home! I am assisting those people. Indeed, for that they

29.text: have called me! Let us return! I will take you with me.” And he really

30.text: takes him along. (For this the man picks up another small splinter, holding

31.text: it with his left hand. This means that the Man from the Upper Region

32.text: brings back the soul, and makes it retrace its way.) At the same time the

33.text: person pronouncing the incantation blows into the right ear and scratches the

34.text: head of the patient. The splinter of wood is put under the pillow of the

35.text: patient. At last the dead one recovers his breath, then his voice comes back

36.text: to him, and then he is able to take a sitting posture. Then the man practising

37.text: the incantation demands from the Morning-Dawn some clothes for the patient.

38.text: He says, “See here! This one is without clothes, this child of mine here!¹

39.text: Give me some clothes, and I will put them on his body.” (He stretches his

40.text: hand upward, as if taking clothes from above.) Then he puts on the clothes,

41.text: and says, “I have put upon you clothes which are unassailable (by the keˊlet).”

42.text: After that they carry the patient back into the house, because, for the last
